questions.summary: Use normal distributions, independence, a travel-time case split, and expectation.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Fiona walks from her house to a bus stop where she gets a bus to school. Her time, W minutes, to walk to the bus stop is normally distributed with W ~ N(12, 3²).

Fiona always leaves her house at 07:15. The first bus that she can get departs at 07:30.

(a) Find the probability that it will take Fiona between 15 minutes and 30 minutes to walk to the bus stop. [2]

The length of time, B minutes, of the bus journey to Fiona’s school is normally distributed with B ~ N(50, σ²). The probability that the bus journey takes less than 60 minutes is 0.941.

(b) Find σ. [3]

(c) Find the probability that the bus journey takes less than 45 minutes. [2]

If Fiona misses the first bus, there is a second bus which departs at 07:45. She must arrive at school by 08:30 to be on time. Fiona will not arrive on time if she misses both buses. The variables W and B are independent.

(d) Find the probability that Fiona will arrive on time. [5]

This year, Fiona will go to school on 183 days.

(e) Calculate the number of days Fiona is expected to arrive on time. [2]
questions.solution: (a) With W ~ N(12, 3²), P(15 < W < 30) = 0.158655… = 0.159. (b) Since P(B < 60) = 0.941, the corresponding standard-normal value is z = 1.56322…. Thus (60 − 50)/σ = 1.56322…, giving σ = 6.39703… = 6.40. (c) Using this σ, P(B < 45) = 0.217221… = 0.217. (d) Fiona is on time either if W ≤ 15 and B < 60, or if 15 < W ≤ 30 and B < 45. By independence, P(on time) = P(W ≤ 15)P(B < 60) + P(15 < W ≤ 30)P(B < 45) = 0.841345…(0.941) + 0.158655…(0.217221…) = 0.826168… = 0.826. (e) The expected number is 183(0.826168…) = 151.188…, hence 151 days.
questions.independentSolution: (a) With W ~ N(12, 3²), P(15 < W < 30) = 0.158655… = 0.159. (b) Since P(B < 60) = 0.941, the corresponding standard-normal value is z = 1.56322…. Thus (60 − 50)/σ = 1.56322…, giving σ = 6.39703… = 6.40. (c) Using this σ, P(B < 45) = 0.217221… = 0.217. (d) Fiona is on time either if W ≤ 15 and B < 60, or if 15 < W ≤ 30 and B < 45. By independence, P(on time) = P(W ≤ 15)P(B < 60) + P(15 < W ≤ 30)P(B < 45) = 0.841345…(0.941) + 0.158655…(0.217221…) = 0.826168… = 0.826. (e) The expected number is 183(0.826168…) = 151.188…, hence 151 days.

Consider a function f(x), for x ≥ 0. The derivative of f is given by f′(x) = 6x/(x² + 4).

(a) Show that f″(x) = (24 − 6x²)/(x² + 4)². [4]

(b) Find the least value of n. [2]

(c) Find ∫ 6x/(x² + 4) dx. [3]

Since the stated region has positive area, ∫₁³f(x) dx = 19.6. Numerically, ∫₁³3ln(x² + 4) dx = 12.4859…, while ∫₁³C dx = 2C. Thus 12.4859… + 2C = 19.6, so C = 3.55700…. Hence f(x) = 3ln(x² + 4) + 3.56 to three significant figures.

questions.summary: Use dice probabilities and an expected-value model to find the least permitted loss amount w for which Ted should stop playing.
questions.accessibleText:
10. [Maximum mark: 16]

Three fair dice each have two green, two yellow and two red faces. (a)(i) Find P(exactly one red); (ii) P(two or more red). [5] Ted wins $10 per green; two or more reds lose all winnings w. (b) Show P(add exactly $10)=1/3. [5] Distribution D: −w,0,10,20,30 with probabilities x,y,1/3,2/9,1/27. (c) Find x,y. [3] The value of w is a positive multiple of 10. (d) Find the least value of w for which Ted should stop playing. [3]
questions.solution: Each colour has probability 1/3. (a) P(R=1)=C(3,1)(1/3)(2/3)²=4/9; P(R≥2)=C(3,2)(1/3)²(2/3)+(1/3)³=7/27. (b) Exactly $10 is added when the dice show one green and either two yellows or one yellow and one red: 3(1/3)³+6(1/3)³=1/3. (c) x=7/27 and y=1−7/27−1/3−2/9−1/27=4/27. (d) E(D)=−7w/27+10/3+40/9+30/27=80/9−7w/27. Ted should stop when E(D)<0, so w>240/7≈34.3. Since w is a positive multiple of 10, the least possible value is $40.

7. [Maximum mark: 8]

Let f(x)=e^(2sin(πx/2)), for x>0. The kth maximum point on the graph of f has x-coordinate xₖ, where k∈ℤ⁺.

(a) Given that xₖ₊₁=xₖ+a, find a. [4]

(b) Hence find the value of n such that ∑(from k=1 to n)xₖ=861. [4]
questions.solution: Because the exponential function is increasing, f is greatest whenever sin(πx/2)=1. Thus πx/2=π/2+2πm, so x=1+4m. Hence x₁=1, x₂=5 and (a) a=4. questions.independentSolution: Because the exponential function is increasing, f is greatest whenever sin(πx/2)=1. Thus πx/2=π/2+2πm, so x=1+4m. Hence x₁=1, x₂=5 and (a) a=4. (b) The xₖ form an arithmetic sequence with xₖ=1+4(k−1). Therefore 861=∑ₖ₌₁ⁿxₖ=n[2+4(n−1)]/2=n(2n−1). Solving 2n²−n−861=0 gives (2n+41)(n−21)=0; since n∈ℤ⁺, n=21.

A city hired 160 employees to work at a festival. The following cumulative frequency curve shows the number of hours employees worked during the festival.

[Graph: Cumulative number of employees, from 0 to 160, plotted against number of hours worked, from 0 to 70. The increasing cumulative frequency curve gives approximately 18 employees at 25 hours, 80 at 40 hours, 130 at 50 hours and 150 at 60 hours.]

(a) (i) Find the median number of hours worked by the employees.

(c) Find the number of employees who earned £200 or less. [3]

10. [Maximum mark: 17]

Let f(x) = x². The following diagram shows part of the graph of f.

[Diagram not to scale: The parabola y=x² contains A(−k,k²). Its tangent L at A descends to the x-axis at B. C=(−k,0), vertically below A.]

The line L is the tangent to the graph of f at the point A(−k, k²), and intersects the x-axis at point B. The point C is (−k, 0).

(a) (i) Write down f′(x).
    (ii) Find the gradient of L. [3]

(b) Show that the x-coordinate of B is −k/2. [5]

(c) Find the area of triangle ABC, giving your answer in terms of k. [2]

The region R is enclosed by L, the graph of f, and the x-axis. [Diagram: R is the region bounded by the parabola from the origin to A, the tangent segment AB, and the x-axis from B to the origin.]

(d) Given that the area of triangle ABC is p times the area of R, find the value of p. [7]

9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Note: distance is in metres and time in seconds. A particle moves for five seconds with acceleration a=3t²−14t+8, for 0≤t≤5.
(a) Write down t when a=0. [2]
(b) Find all t for which velocity is decreasing. [2]
At t=0 velocity is 3 m s⁻¹. (c) Find velocity v(t). [6]
(d) Find total distance travelled when velocity is increasing. [4]
questions.solution: 3t²−14t+8=(3t−2)(t−4), so a=0 at t=2/3 and 4. Velocity decreases where a<0, namely 2/3<t<4. Integrating, v=t³−7t²+8t+C; v(0)=3 gives v=t³−7t²+8t+3. Velocity increases on 0<t<2/3 and 4<t<5. Integrating |v| over these intervals (splitting where needed) gives total distance 14.2191≈14.2 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics SL
questions.summary: Analyze a periodic saw-tooth model and count complete teeth.
questions.accessibleText:
10. [Maximum mark: 17]

Note: In this question, distance is in millimetres.

Let f(x)=x+a sin(x−π/2)+a, for x≥0.

(a) Show that f(2π)=2π. [3]

The graph of f passes through the origin. Let P_k be any point on the graph of f with x-coordinate 2kπ, where k∈ℕ. A straight line L passes through all the points P_k.

(b) (i) Find the coordinates of P₀ and of P₁.
    (ii) Find the equation of L. [6]

(c) Show that the distance between the x-coordinates of P_k and P_(k+1) is 2π. [2]

Diagram 1 shows a saw. The length of the toothed edge is the distance AB. The toothed edge of the saw can be modelled using the graph of f and the line L, as represented in Diagram 2.

[Diagram 1, not to scale: A saw whose straight toothed edge runs from A to B.]

[Diagram 2, not to scale: Coordinate axes labelled distance (in mm). The line L rises from the origin and the periodic graph of f forms a sequence of arches above L, meeting L at consecutive points P_k and P_(k+1). The shaded region enclosed by f and L between P_k and P_(k+1) is labelled tooth.]

The shaded part on the graph is called a tooth. A tooth is represented by the region enclosed by the graph of f and the line L, between P_k and P_(k+1).

(d) A saw has a toothed edge which is 300 mm long. Find the number of complete teeth on this saw. [6]
questions.solution: f(2π)=2π+a sin(3π/2)+a=2π. At multiples 2kπ, sin(2kπ−π/2)=−1, so P_k=(2kπ,2kπ). Thus P₀=(0,0), P₁=(2π,2π), and L is y=x. Consecutive x-coordinates differ 2(k+1)π−2kπ=2π. Since the 300 mm toothed edge is modelled in the direction of L, its horizontal projection is 300/√2 mm. Dividing this by the horizontal width 2π of one tooth gives 300/(2π√2)=33.7618, so the saw has 33 complete teeth.
questions.independentSolution: f(2π)=2π+a sin(3π/2)+a=2π. At multiples 2kπ, sin(2kπ−π/2)=−1, so P_k=(2kπ,2kπ). Thus P₀=(0,0), P₁=(2π,2π), and L is y=x. Consecutive x-coordinates differ 2(k+1)π−2kπ=2π. Since the 300 mm toothed edge is modelled in the direction of L, its horizontal projection is 300/√2 mm. Dividing this by the horizontal width 2π of one tooth gives 300/(2π√2)=33.7618, so the saw has 33 complete teeth.
